card.title: Basicity and diazotisation — the lone pair at work

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Amines are ammonia's alkyl/aryl children (1°/2°/3° by carbon count on N); the lone pair makes them bases and nucleophiles — alkyl groups boost basicity (+I) while aromatic delocalisation bleeds it away (aniline ≪ aliphatic amines). Primary aromatic amines diazotise at 0–5 °C into Ar–N₂⁺Cl⁻, the gateway to azo dyes (coupling) and replacement chemistry. Hinsberg (benzenesulphonyl chloride) sorts 1°/2°/3° by sulphonamide solubility.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: basicity (aqueous): 2° > 1° > 3° > NH₃ > aniline (solvation + +I + resonance balance)  ·  diazotisation: Ar–NH₂ + NaNO₂/HCl, 0–5 °C → Ar–N₂⁺Cl⁻  ·  coupling: Ar–N₂⁺ + phenol/amine → azo dye (p-position)  ·  Hinsberg: 1° soluble → 2° insoluble → 3° no reaction

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Diazotisation demands 0–5 °C (diazonium salts detonate/decompose warm) and excess mineral acid. Coupling runs alkaline (phenols) or weakly acidic (amines) at the para position. Aqueous basicity orders need solvation factored — gas-phase orders differ (then +I rules alone).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Aniline is ~10⁶× weaker base than cyclohexylamine (lone pair delocalised into the ring). Diazonium replacement gives phenol (boil/H₂O), chlorobenzene (Sandmeyer CuCl), fluorobenzene (Schiemann), iodobenzene (KI) — one intermediate, a whole catalogue. Carbylamine stench-marks primary amines (CHCl₃/KOH test).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Rank: diethylamine > ethylamine > trimethylamine > ammonia > aniline (aqueous). Logic: +I boosts with alkylation, but 3° solvates poorly (fewer H-bonds to NH⁺), and aniline's pair is ring-delocalised. Hinsberg check: 1° sulphonamide dissolves in NaOH (acidic N–H), 2° does not, 3° never reacts.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Basicity orders flip between gas phase, water and DMSO — always specify medium. Diazonium chemistry needs cold, fresh reagents (stale salt = tar). Over-alkylation plagues direct amination (mixtures of 1°/2°/3°/quaternary) — Gabriel phthalimide fixes it for primary amines.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Basicity from conjugate-acid stability + lone-pair availability: alkyl +I raises electron density (stronger base) until solvation of bulkier ammonium ions falls behind — the 2° maximum derived, not memorised. Diazotisation: HNO₂ nitrosonium attacks Ar–NH₂ → N-nitroso → diazonium after dehydration; resonance (Ar–N⁺≡N ↔ Ar–N=N⁺) explains aryl stability vs alkyl diazonium collapse.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Aqueous basicity chant: 2° > 1° > 3° > NH₃ ≫ aniline. Diazo conditions: 0–5 °C, NaNO₂/HCl — write them every time. Azo coupling at para (or ortho if blocked). Hinsberg: soluble/insoluble/none for 1°/2°/3°.
